thread:
ops-bot: alert: spike detected — 429 responses for POST /v1/rerank from api-key acme-prod-01 (window: 60s, 429s: 312)
jen_support: putting this thread together for acme support ticket #7891 — customer says sudden 429s since ~10:12 UTC, affecting rerank only. Sam, can you paste a repro / example payload?
sam_acme: yep — here's the simplified curl we used (we hit 429 immediately):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer acme-prod-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"best product","candidates":["id1","id2",...,(500 total)]}'
```
sam_acme: our frontend sends ~500 candidates per request after client-side expansion. We expect server to rerank; latency is okay but we see lots of 429 and clients retrying, making it worse.
jen_support: thanks — that helps. Do you have any response headers from the 429? any x-retry-after or request-id?
sam_acme: one example response body: `{"error":"rate_limited","message":"too many requests"}` and header `Retry-After: 8` and `X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d`.
mika_eng: quick note on how rerank metering works — each candidate counts as an internal unit for quota when computed. Large candidate arrays literally multiply the token/execution footprint; 500 candidates is ~10-20x a normal call depending on scoring model. Rate limiter is per-api-key + per-route (we throttle rerank stricter), using a leaky-bucket with burst smoothing. If you send large batches repeatedly, token bucket drains and you get sustained 429s.
jordan_sre: log excerpt for that request id: `2026-03-16T10:12:15Z req_0a1b2c3d POST /v1/rerank 500candidates -> 429 quota_exceeded key=acme-prod-01 tokens_needed=480 tokens_available=0`.
jen_support: suggested immediate mitigations for the customer?
mika_eng: short term: reduce candidates per call to <=50, or pre-filter client-side to top-k before hitting rerank. Also implement exponential backoff with jitter (we saw their clients currently retry every 1s). Example backoff: base=500ms, multiply by 2, jitter ±20%. Also respect `Retry-After` header.
jordan_sre: ops can also issue a temporary quota smoothing/burst bump while customer rolls out fixes. I can grant a 24h rate override. Command I used: `rb-admin quota adjust --key acme-prod-01 --route rerank --burst 3x --duration 24h` (internal only).
kevin_sales: customer asked for a faster fix — please confirm if we can do the bump now, they say revenue impact.
jordan_sre: applied: 3x burst smoothing for 24h, note logged as change-id chg_20260316_45. Monitoring: 429 rate dropped ~70% immediately but still elevated because client-side retries kept generating traffic.
sam_acme: we rolled out a partial fix — reduce candidate list to 40 in search pipeline and enabled backoff. After ~10 minutes error rate dropped to near zero. Thanks.
mika_eng: follow-ups — we should add clearer docs on candidate counting and recommended client-side limits, and consider returning a 4xx-specific error `candidate_count_exceeded` for >1000 rather than generic 429 so clients can fail fast. Also we want to add a per-request header `X-Candidate-Count` so we can surface more helpful quota diagnostics in telemetry.
jen_support: I'll log a product doc update and follow up with the customer to confirm acceptance of the temporary quota and timeline. Also creating internal ticket to add `X-Candidate-Count` and the explicit 4xx for overlarge payloads.
jordan_sre: pending action: close after 24h check. change-id chg_20260316_45, internal ticket TKT-1159.
jen_support: closing thread here — customer resolved with reduced candidate size and our 24h burst. Reopen if anything recurs. :white_check_mark:
